object_description: dominant trapezoidal volume perforated by inner courtyards
design_condition: The large volume occupies the full site in its final phase, preserves neighbouring buildings during the first phase, and organizes public access through a major courtyard while creating dynamic street spaces around the perimeter.

positive.statement: The clear urban development stance creates dynamic street spaces all around.
The first stage is cleverly designed so that neighbouring buildings can be preserved temporarily.
Access to all uses via the courtyard and foyer is functionally well solved.
The internal access is clearly arranged through the foyer and flanking access towers.
The campus hall is functionally optimal and can be flexibly adapted to user requirements.
The regular grid does justice to the wooden construction and enables efficient manufacture of the ceiling system.
The building shell is pleasantly proportioned, and the screen gives the large volume a pleasant vertical structure.

negative.statement: The project heavily occupies public space and has high dominance in the urban space.
The design of the open spaces, inner courtyards and street spaces has not yet been exhausted.
The public space inside the complex is shaded and offers few qualities.
The functionality for the school is highly doubted.
The natural lighting of the offices and lounges is reduced, and the clear view down is likely to be unpleasant for library users.
The corridors sometimes appear longer than average and have hardly any spatial qualities.
The floor-to-ceiling glazing could restrict workplaces directly on the building shell.
The large-scale volume and screen appear too closed and somewhat alien in the urban space.
